newsitem.title: LEBANON: South Lebanon shelling wounds Lebanese orphan.
newsitem.headline: South Lebanon shelling wounds Lebanese orphan.

text.p: A five-year-old Lebanese girl was wounded on Sunday when a shell hit an orphanage in south Lebanon, Lebanese security sources said.

They said the shell -- fired from an unknown direction -- struck the SOS orphanage in Kfar Falous in the Jizzine area, officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under the control of the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.
Hasna Mohamed Kataneh was wounded in the attack.
Earlier, a mine exploded near a truck in the village of Marqaba inside the occupation zone. No one was injured in the blast, according to SLA militia sources.
This week, 14 Lebanese including seven civilians have been killed in Israeli shelling, air raids or bombs planted by unknown assailants.
It was the worst episode of cross-border violence in more than 15 months when Israel launched a 17-day blitz on the country, killing some 200 Lebanese -- mostly civilians.
Israel, backed by the SLA, control a buffer strip in south Lebanon which it craved out in 1985 to stop cross-border guerrilla attacks into its northern borders.
